Q: Excel Lookup Returning Date Values A:

Select the F column in the main tab and set its cell format to General or Number.

Q: HTTP Error 500.1000 - Internal Server Error A:

The probelm may be related to permissions, you can try to set application pool identity to NetworkService or LocalSystem.

  1. Go to Application Pools. Select your application.
  2. Click on Advance Settings.
  3. Change Indentity to NetworkService or LocalSystem

Q: Problem with openjdk-21 changing font character widths A:

The problem turns out to be that a different font is chosen by Java for "Serif" than what the system provides during postscript rendering/printing. I have not tracked down exactly where this is happening, but presumably it is somewhere in the Java or Ubuntu font configuration files. What is specifically happening is that Java is instantiating "Noto Serif" or possibly "DejaVu Serif", both of which are "bulkier" than the "Nimbus Roman" that is chosen by postscript. There are also some odd values for font metrics from Java in these cases, where the bounding rectangle height is not the font size + leading (in fact, leading is 0). If I specify a physical font (e.g. "NimbusRoman-Regular") then Java embeds the character glyphs as drawing commands and so there is no dependency on system fonts after that - however the postscript file is significantly larger. When portability is of concern (exporting the postscript to other systems), using logical fonts may not be desirable anyway.

Q: Setting Subplot Height/Width A:

I've found some solution (maybe not the best but, at least, it is something). layout's height property may be used together with setFixedHeight property of a plot.

Example of usage:

indPlot.setFixedHeight(layout.height() * 0.25)
